At Regeneron, we use science and innovation to develop life-changing medicines for people with serious diseases. We are seeking an Executive Director
to join our Patient Safety
team.

The Executive Director, Global Patient Safety Sciences Delivery serves as the key point of contact for all Safety Sciences operations and risk-related responsibilities across all Therapeutic Areas (TAs). This role is responsible for driving consistency across the portfolio for standard activities performed by the Safety Scientists (e.g., data transformation, safety surveillance, SMT preparation, early draft of aggregate reports, signal evaluations, label enhancement justifications). This role is also responsible for the processes and written procedures that underpin the safety governance, and other fundamental processes within Safety Sciences. This role requires the ability to work cross-functionally, partnering with the Safety Sciences TAHs and other leaders. They will serve as a member of the GPS Leadership Team (GPS LT). The Executive Director, Global Patient Safety Sciences Delivery is also responsible for the development and management of their team.

This position offers the opportunity to contribute to a fast-growing, science-driven organization making a meaningful difference to patients worldwide.

When & Where

Work Location: Tarrytown, NY, Warren, NJ or Cambridge, MA
4 days per week onsite
Travel: As needed

Define the strategy to ensure standardization and consistency in execution of core activities (e.g., signal detection, authoring sections for safety documents) across all products and TAs through development of common practices, processes, templates
Oversee relevant training programs for GPS Safety Sciences, including a standardized training curriculum, proficiency matrix, and knowledge management repository
Enable the Global Capability Center (GCC) to operate more efficiency and scale with the demands of the business
Develop innovative approaches to delivering on core activities that integrate in new technologies, including AI

Oversee all aspects of signal detection coordination and signal management process across all TAs, including Safety Monitoring Team (SMT), Safety Surveillance Plan (SSP) and Signal Evaluation Report (SER)

Partner with key Regeneron interfaces (e.g., Clinical, Regulatory, Med Affairs, Biostats & Data Management)

Talent Development & Organizational Leadership

Build, coach, and scale a high-performing team, and drive succession planning and talent pipelines
Lead talent strategy and leadership development initiatives that strengthen capabilities across the organization.

Minimum M.D., PA, PhD or PharmD Degree; Board Certification or equivalent in relevant clinical specialty, MBA is an advantage.
17+ years total experience in PV or relevant clinical experience in the pharmaceutical industry required
6+ years of leading a team and people management experience
Preferred experience with oversight of operations within a global patient safety organization

We continually aspire and invest in learning and development opportunities that support our team members’ professional growth, ensuring every team member has the tools to build a meaningful and rewarding career.

Executive Director
to join our community.

jobs.description:
About Sage Bionetworks

Sage Bionetworks is a nonprofit biomedical research and technology organization that advances human health through open science and collaborative discovery. We work at the intersection of biomedical science, data, technology, and patient engagement - partnering across academia, industry, philanthropy, and government to build research programs, data resources, and technology that accelerate scientific progress.

Sage brings particular expertise in collaborative research, multimodal biomedical data, responsible data governance, and open source technology. As an AI forward organization, we are also exploring how emerging technologies can responsibly expand the reach and impact of scientific data and discovery.

The Opportunity

Sage Bionetworks is seeking a Director of Partnerships to help shape and grow our work beyond our historically government funded portfolio. This is a scientific leadership and partnership role
and not a traditional business development or sales role
. We are looking for someone with hands-on training and/or experience in biomedical data and technology who can develop partnerships with pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical technology, health technology, AI companies, as well as foundations and other mission aligned organizations.

Successful partnerships at Sage begin with substantive scientific and technical conversations. The Director must be able to engage scientists, technical leaders, and executives as a credible peer, understand what they are trying to accomplish, and translate that understanding into a focused opportunity that draws on Sage’s distinctive capabilities.

Our mission is to break silos in biomedical research and drive a new age of discovery through truly open science and radical collaboration. The Director will work across organizational boundaries to connect three things: the challenges and opportunities emerging in the external market, the underlying needs of prospective partners, and the scientific and technical capabilities Sage is best positioned to provide. Dyne Therapeutics is focused on delivering functional improvement for people living with genetically driven neuromuscular diseases. We are developing therapeutics that target muscle and the central nervous system (CNS) to address the root cause of disease. Role Summary

The Executive Director, Portfolio Analytics & Systems Architecture is a strategic enterprise leader who reports into Portfolio Strategy & Operations and serves as the Operational Data and Technology Business Partner. The leader is responsible for designing, building, and scaling a state-of-the-art reporting, analytics, and insights capability across our clinical development portfolio, while architecting and leading the delivery of the operational data systems architecture that underpins it in partnership with the IT/Digital team. This role establishes a single source of truth for clinical study, program, and portfolio performance; delivers trusted time, cost, and quality insights; infuses AI across clinical study, program and portfolio processes and systems; and enables confident, data-driven decisions by study teams, functional leaders, governance bodies and executive team. As the corresponding IT Business Partner, the leader translates functional strategy into a coherent systems and data roadmap, designs enterprise data models, and works closely with IT/Digital counterparts to deliver, integrate, and sustain validated clinical systems. The leader will partner closely with R&D functions, such as Portfolio and Program Management, Clinical Operations, Biometrics, as well as Commercial, Finance, HR/Workforce Planning, and IT/Digital to implement a modern operational data infrastructure and advanced analytics—spanning descriptive to prescriptive (AI/ML)—that improves predictability, optimizes resources, and accelerates medicines to patients.

Enterprise Data & Insights Strategy

Design, define, and advance a next-generation insights platform that delivers trusted, real-time reporting and analytics across studies, programs, and the portfolio—enabling monitoring of time, cost, and quality and supporting decision-making from study and program teams to the Executive Committee and Board.
Establish and govern one “source of truth” by integrating internal and external operational data (e.g., CROs and vendor feeds, benchmarking sources) into a harmonized model with robust data quality, lineage, and access controls.

Data Foundation & Technology Enablement

Serve as the primary technology leader and business partner to Portfolio and Program Management and Clinical with a focus on data, portfolio and analytics systems, and clinical systems architecture and operations, building strong relationships with senior leadership and stakeholders to understand business objectives, priorities, and technology and process needs and gaps.
In close partnership with IT/Digital, architect a centralized operational data infrastructure (e.g., data lake/warehouse, semantic layer, data products) that powers consistent analytics and self-service business intelligence.
Integrate operational planning data (study/program plans, budgets, baselines) with actuals to enable accurate planned vs. actual comparisons for timelines and costs.
Implement scalable operational data governance (metadata, master data, standards) aligned with R&D operating models and GxP expectations.
Serve as the primary IT liaison for Portfolio and Analytics teams and across clinical and R&D teams, translating business needs into actionable technology solutions.
Lead the delivery, support, and continuous improvement of business technology platforms (e.g., Portfolio Management tools, clinical systems, and portfolio and analytics tools), ensuring they are robust and scalable.

Analytics, KPIs & Methodologies

Develop streamlined, standard analytical frameworks and methodologies (definitions, metric specifications, visualization standards) to drive consistency and comparability across the organization.
Define and operationalize clinical study, program, and portfolio KPIs (e.g., cycle times, site activation and enrollment velocity, budget adherence, deviation/quality indicators, vendor performance, milestone attainment) and performance analytics.
Lead the creation of advanced analytics and simulation capabilities to predict and optimize development timelines, costs, and risks (e.g., slippage forecasting, patient enrollment trajectories, budget risks, operational risks), including evaluation of operational implications.

AI-Enabled Prescriptive Insights

Design and deploy prescriptive analytics powered by AI/ML that anticipate study, program, and portfolio-level challenges and provide actionable recommendations (e.g., mitigation strategies, scenario trade-offs, risk flags, next-best actions)
Enable portfolio-wide scenario modeling and resource planning, supporting governance decision-making (e.g., start/stop/sequence, trade-offs, capacity constraints and resource supply)

Country/Site Intelligence & Study Delivery

Develop predictive country and site selection analytics to optimize trial delivery (start-up speed, enrollment yield, data quality, cost) and inform feasibility and country footprint decisions.
Establish a study-level insights platform that leverages structured operational data to provide site- and PI-level insights (enrollment health, quality, cost, competitive trial density) to study teams and vendor partners.

Resource Management & Capacity Planning

Design and institutionalize an integrated resource management capability that dynamically analyzes resource demand vs. actuals across the portfolio; predicts AI-enabled resource demand; and highlights capacity bottlenecks for scarce skills/roles in close partnership with HR and functional leaders.

Operating Model, Change & Adoption

Drive change management and adoption of new analytics capabilities, ensuring insights are embedded in business rhythms (governance reviews, QBRs, portfolio prioritization, study health checks).
Lead with Compliance and Trust—embedding regulatory compliance (e.g., GxP, GDPR) into every solution, safeguarding our data and maintaining Dyne’s reputation for integrity.
Be a champion of innovation--Identifying emerging technologies that can elevate Dyne’s R&D capabilities and portfolio management and operational insights strategies.
Bring forward ideas that challenge the status quo and deliver measurable business impact.

Education And Skills Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in quantitative or life sciences field (e.g., Statistics, Data Science, Engineering, Operations Research, Epidemiology, Pharmacy, Biology). Preferred: Master’s or PhD in Data Science, Biostatistics, Operations Research, or related discipline; MBA a plus
18+ years of increasing responsibility in biopharma/biotech R&D with a focus on clinical operations analytics, portfolio management, or development operations, including 5+ years leading multi-disciplinary teams
Proven track record building enterprise data & analytics platforms and single source of truth solutions for R&D portfolios, integrating internal and external/vendor data (e.g., CRO feeds, benchmarks)
Demonstrated expertise with portfolio, program, and study KPIs, operational planning and plan vs. actual analysis, and scenario modeling for timelines, costs, risks, and resources
Hands-on experience with advanced analytics/ML (forecasting, simulation, optimization) and turning algorithms into operational tools that drive business decisions
Strong understanding of the clinical development lifecycle, including feasibility, site activation, enrollment, data management, monitoring, and close-out; familiarity with GCP/GxP, data privacy, and validation expectations for decision-support tools
Executive presence with the ability to influence senior stakeholders (Governance/EC), translate complex analytics into clear narratives, and drive enterprise alignment
Collaborative corporate leader who partners effectively with other senior leaders to advance the company’s mission and portfolio
Exceptional ability to influence without direct authority across all organizational levels, including senior functional leaders
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to convey complex information clearly to diverse audiences (written, verbal and presentation)
Ability to interpret and communicate complex data to diverse audiences
As a plus:
experience with site/country selection analytics, enrollment prediction, and vendor performance analytics
Familiarity with R&D systems (e.g., CTMS, EDC, eTMF, RTSM, safety, eCOA), portfolio/financial planning (e.g., enterprise planning tools), and HR capacity planning

Positive team member who embodies Dyne’s Core Values

About Sage Bionetworks

Sage Bionetworks is a nonprofit biomedical research and technology organization that advances human health through open science and collaborative discovery. We work at the intersection of biomedical science, data, technology, and patient engagement - partnering across academia, industry, philanthropy, and government to build research programs, data resources, and technology that accelerate scientific progress.

Sage brings particular expertise in collaborative research, multimodal biomedical data, responsible data governance, and open source technology. As an AI forward organization, we are also exploring how emerging technologies can responsibly expand the reach and impact of scientific data and discovery.

The Opportunity

Sage Bionetworks is seeking a Director of Partnerships to help shape and grow our work beyond our historically government funded portfolio. This is a scientific leadership and partnership role
and not a traditional business development or sales role
. We are looking for someone with hands-on training and/or experience in biomedical data and technology who can develop partnerships with pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical technology, health technology, AI companies, as well as foundations and other mission aligned organizations.

Successful partnerships at Sage begin with substantive scientific and technical conversations. The Director must be able to engage scientists, technical leaders, and executives as a credible peer, understand what they are trying to accomplish, and translate that understanding into a focused opportunity that draws on Sage’s distinctive capabilities.

Our mission is to break silos in biomedical research and drive a new age of discovery through truly open science and radical collaboration. The Director will work across organizational boundaries to connect three things: the challenges and opportunities emerging in the external market, the underlying needs of prospective partners, and the scientific and technical capabilities Sage is best positioned to provide. They will work closely with Sage’s CEO and Chief Data Officer to help Sage define clearer, repeatable partnership offerings while ensuring that individual opportunities remain aligned with our mission, strategy, capabilities, and capacity.

The Director will also lead scientific and technical discovery and develop strategic initiatives that demonstrate Sage’s capabilities and increase its visibility. They will directly (hands on) contribute analyses, prototypes, demonstrations, and business cases that advance partnership opportunities and position Sage for future funding.

You Will Succeed at Sage If You

Combine your scientific and technical depth with strong commercial and strategic judgment, moving comfortably across scientific, operational, and executive conversations.
Listen for the need beneath a partner’s initial request and translate it into a focused, feasible, and reusable solution.
Are proactive, resourceful, and accountable, willing to do substantive work yourself and use data, technology, and AI to create momentum amid ambiguity.
Build trust through curiosity and collaboration while constructively challenging assumptions and balancing partner needs with Sage’s mission, strategy, and capacity.

You’ll Know You’re Succeeding When

Sage has a clear external partnership strategy and a focused portfolio of compelling, repeatable solutions grounded in its scientific and technical strengths.
New and existing relationships with priority organizations are advancing into deeper, longer term, and funded partnerships.
Opportunities are translated into appropriately simple, valuable, and feasible solutions, with Sage’s internal teams aligned and engaged at the right time.
The partnership portfolio strengthens Sage’s reputation as a scientific and technical collaborator and contributes meaningfully to revenue diversification and mission impact.

Key Responsibilities

Partnership and market strategy

Develop and grow a diversified portfolio of new and existing external partnerships across pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical technology, health technology, AI, and philanthropic organizations.
Identify scientific, technological and market developments that create opportunities for Sage’s research, data, governance, and technology capabilities.
Build relationships with scientific, technical, executive, and funding decision-makers, translating priority relationships into a qualified pipeline of proposals and funded agreements.

Defining solutions and offerings

Develop a clear portfolio of compelling, repeatable solutions that connect external needs with Sage’s distinctive scientific, data, governance, technology, and AI capabilities.
Evaluate and shape opportunities based on strategic alignment, scientific value, differentiation, feasibility, funding potential, and organizational capacity
Bring insights from partners and the broader market into Sage to inform organizational strategy, capability development, and investment priorities.
Work closely with the CEO, Chief Data Officer, and other organizational leaders to shape Sage’s partnership strategy and identify priority sectors, organizations, and opportunities

Scientific and technical Discovery

Lead hands on discovery with prospective partners to understand their scientific questions, data, technical environments, constraints, and intended outcomes.
Apply practical expertise in biomedical data, research workflows, analytics, and AI to develop credible solution concepts, analyses, prototypes, demonstrations, and proofs of concept.
Identify, build the business case for, and lead strategic initiatives (for example, community engagement efforts, scientific challenges, pilots, and analyses) that strengthen Sage’s capabilities, increase its visibility, and position it for future partnerships and funding.
Lead the scientific strategy and content for external scientific events, including Sage’s flagship event (Sage Assembly) by developing compelling themes, speakers, and programming that showcase Sage’s capabilities, advance its mission, and strengthen relationships with priority partners.

Proposal development and internal alignment

Serve as the bridge between external partners and Sage’s scientific, technical, operational, and leadership teams, creating a shared understanding of partner needs, Sage’s capabilities, and key constraints.
Lead the development of realistic concept notes, proposals, presentations, scopes and budgets, driving toward practical solutions and avoiding unnecessary complexity or customization.
Facilitate decisions about priorities, resources, risks, and tradeoffs, ensuring commitments are strategically aligned and transition clearly into delivery.

People leadership and mentorship

Build trusted relationships with Sage’s principal investigators and scientific, technical, and operational leaders, fostering collaboration across disciplines.
Mentor colleagues and emerging leaders through context-sharing, constructive feedback, and opportunities to develop their capabilities and visibility.
Build and lead a team over time, aligned with the growth and needs of Sage’s partnership portfolio.

Qualifications

Education

Advanced degree in a biomedical, behavioral, public health, data science, engineering, or related discipline.
A PhD or equivalent scientific leadership and industry experience is strongly preferred

Experience

Significant experience (10+ years) across biomedical science, data, technology, and external partnerships.
Demonstrated success originating and advancing funded partnerships with life science, health technology, or AI organizations.
Experience translating partner needs into focused solutions and developing the proposals, scopes, budgets, agreements, and negotiations needed to move opportunities forward.
Hands on experience with health data and data intensive technologies; AI/ML experience preferred.
Strong scientific communication, cross functional relationship building, and an established industry network.
Sound judgment, personal accountability, and the ability to advance opportunities amid ambiguity.

Nice to Have

Experience working with multimodal biomedical and health data, including clinical, observational, molecular, imaging, and patient generated data.
Familiarity with biomedical data governance, open science practices, FAIR principles, and responsible AI.
Experience with data partnerships, platform licensing, strategic alliances, or other models beyond fee for service work.
Experience using AI coding agents, such as Claude Code, to analyze data, prototype solutions, or accelerate technical work.

new_jobs.title: Executive Director, Portfolio Analytics & Systems Architecture
new_jobs.description:
Company Overview

Dyne Therapeutics is focused on delivering functional improvement for people living with genetically driven neuromuscular diseases. We are developing therapeutics that target muscle and the central nervous system (CNS) to address the root cause of disease. The company is advancing clinical programs for Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) and myotonic dystrophy type 1 (DM1) as well as preclinical programs for facioscapulohumeral muscular dystrophy (FSHD), Pompe disease and multiple DMD mutations. At Dyne, we are on a mission to deliver functional improvement for individuals, families and communities. Learn more at https://www.dyne-tx.com/, and follow us on X, LinkedIn and Facebook.

Role Summary

The Executive Director, Portfolio Analytics & Systems Architecture is a strategic enterprise leader who reports into Portfolio Strategy & Operations and serves as the Operational Data and Technology Business Partner. The leader is responsible for designing, building, and scaling a state-of-the-art reporting, analytics, and insights capability across our clinical development portfolio, while architecting and leading the delivery of the operational data systems architecture that underpins it in partnership with the IT/Digital team. This role establishes a single source of truth for clinical study, program, and portfolio performance; delivers trusted time, cost, and quality insights; infuses AI across clinical study, program and portfolio processes and systems; and enables confident, data-driven decisions by study teams, functional leaders, governance bodies and executive team. As the corresponding IT Business Partner, the leader translates functional strategy into a coherent systems and data roadmap, designs enterprise data models, and works closely with IT/Digital counterparts to deliver, integrate, and sustain validated clinical systems. The leader will partner closely with R&D functions, such as Portfolio and Program Management, Clinical Operations, Biometrics, as well as Commercial, Finance, HR/Workforce Planning, and IT/Digital to implement a modern operational data infrastructure and advanced analytics—spanning descriptive to prescriptive (AI/ML)—that improves predictability, optimizes resources, and accelerates medicines to patients.

This role is based in Waltham, MA.

Primary Responsibilities Include

Enterprise Data & Insights Strategy

Design, define, and advance a next-generation insights platform that delivers trusted, real-time reporting and analytics across studies, programs, and the portfolio—enabling monitoring of time, cost, and quality and supporting decision-making from study and program teams to the Executive Committee and Board.
Establish and govern one “source of truth” by integrating internal and external operational data (e.g., CROs and vendor feeds, benchmarking sources) into a harmonized model with robust data quality, lineage, and access controls.

Data Foundation & Technology Enablement

Serve as the primary technology leader and business partner to Portfolio and Program Management and Clinical with a focus on data, portfolio and analytics systems, and clinical systems architecture and operations, building strong relationships with senior leadership and stakeholders to understand business objectives, priorities, and technology and process needs and gaps.
In close partnership with IT/Digital, architect a centralized operational data infrastructure (e.g., data lake/warehouse, semantic layer, data products) that powers consistent analytics and self-service business intelligence.
Integrate operational planning data (study/program plans, budgets, baselines) with actuals to enable accurate planned vs. actual comparisons for timelines and costs.
Implement scalable operational data governance (metadata, master data, standards) aligned with R&D operating models and GxP expectations.
Serve as the primary IT liaison for Portfolio and Analytics teams and across clinical and R&D teams, translating business needs into actionable technology solutions.
Lead the delivery, support, and continuous improvement of business technology platforms (e.g., Portfolio Management tools, clinical systems, and portfolio and analytics tools), ensuring they are robust and scalable.

Analytics, KPIs & Methodologies

Develop streamlined, standard analytical frameworks and methodologies (definitions, metric specifications, visualization standards) to drive consistency and comparability across the organization.
Define and operationalize clinical study, program, and portfolio KPIs (e.g., cycle times, site activation and enrollment velocity, budget adherence, deviation/quality indicators, vendor performance, milestone attainment) and performance analytics.
Lead the creation of advanced analytics and simulation capabilities to predict and optimize development timelines, costs, and risks (e.g., slippage forecasting, patient enrollment trajectories, budget risks, operational risks), including evaluation of operational implications.

AI-Enabled Prescriptive Insights

Design and deploy prescriptive analytics powered by AI/ML that anticipate study, program, and portfolio-level challenges and provide actionable recommendations (e.g., mitigation strategies, scenario trade-offs, risk flags, next-best actions)
Enable portfolio-wide scenario modeling and resource planning, supporting governance decision-making (e.g., start/stop/sequence, trade-offs, capacity constraints and resource supply)

Country/Site Intelligence & Study Delivery

Develop predictive country and site selection analytics to optimize trial delivery (start-up speed, enrollment yield, data quality, cost) and inform feasibility and country footprint decisions.
Establish a study-level insights platform that leverages structured operational data to provide site- and PI-level insights (enrollment health, quality, cost, competitive trial density) to study teams and vendor partners.

Resource Management & Capacity Planning

Design and institutionalize an integrated resource management capability that dynamically analyzes resource demand vs. actuals across the portfolio; predicts AI-enabled resource demand; and highlights capacity bottlenecks for scarce skills/roles in close partnership with HR and functional leaders.

Operating Model, Change & Adoption

Drive change management and adoption of new analytics capabilities, ensuring insights are embedded in business rhythms (governance reviews, QBRs, portfolio prioritization, study health checks).
Lead with Compliance and Trust—embedding regulatory compliance (e.g., GxP, GDPR) into every solution, safeguarding our data and maintaining Dyne’s reputation for integrity.
Be a champion of innovation--Identifying emerging technologies that can elevate Dyne’s R&D capabilities and portfolio management and operational insights strategies.
Bring forward ideas that challenge the status quo and deliver measurable business impact.

Education And Skills Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in quantitative or life sciences field (e.g., Statistics, Data Science, Engineering, Operations Research, Epidemiology, Pharmacy, Biology). Preferred: Master’s or PhD in Data Science, Biostatistics, Operations Research, or related discipline; MBA a plus
18+ years of increasing responsibility in biopharma/biotech R&D with a focus on clinical operations analytics, portfolio management, or development operations, including 5+ years leading multi-disciplinary teams
Proven track record building enterprise data & analytics platforms and single source of truth solutions for R&D portfolios, integrating internal and external/vendor data (e.g., CRO feeds, benchmarks)
Demonstrated expertise with portfolio, program, and study KPIs, operational planning and plan vs. actual analysis, and scenario modeling for timelines, costs, risks, and resources
Hands-on experience with advanced analytics/ML (forecasting, simulation, optimization) and turning algorithms into operational tools that drive business decisions
Strong understanding of the clinical development lifecycle, including feasibility, site activation, enrollment, data management, monitoring, and close-out; familiarity with GCP/GxP, data privacy, and validation expectations for decision-support tools
Executive presence with the ability to influence senior stakeholders (Governance/EC), translate complex analytics into clear narratives, and drive enterprise alignment
Collaborative corporate leader who partners effectively with other senior leaders to advance the company’s mission and portfolio
Exceptional ability to influence without direct authority across all organizational levels, including senior functional leaders
Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to convey complex information clearly to diverse audiences (written, verbal and presentation)
Ability to interpret and communicate complex data to diverse audiences
As a plus:
experience with site/country selection analytics, enrollment prediction, and vendor performance analytics
Familiarity with R&D systems (e.g., CTMS, EDC, eTMF, RTSM, safety, eCOA), portfolio/financial planning (e.g., enterprise planning tools), and HR capacity planning
Background in data governance (metadata, MDM), data product management, and adoption at scale

Excellent team player
Strong decision maker
Ability to work in a matrix environment
Ability to work independently as a hands-on manager, proactively contribute as a resource when necessary
Flexibility to adapt and meet the changing/growing needs of our customers
High level of integrity, compliance, ethics, and transparency
Positive team member who embodies Dyne’s Core Values
Excitement about Dyne’s vision and mission
